previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple myeloma, chronic hemolytic anemia, type 2 diabetes, and stage V chronic kidney disease, was admitted for worsening lower extremity edema and 12-pound weight gain despite optimized diuretic therapy. He was started on IV furosemide, received two units of packed red blood cells for anemia, and was initiated on hemodialysis after placement of a tunneled dialysis catheter. He completed three dialysis sessions, lost 22 pounds, and showed improvement in renal function and volume status. His C. difficile infection was managed with a tapering course of oral vancomycin, and vitamin D deficiency was addressed with weekly supplementation. He was discharged home with services, continuing dialysis, diuretics, and close follow-up.

COMPARISON:  Cervical spine radiograph of ___, CT chest, abdomen and

FINDINGS: 

CERVICAL:
Cervical alignment is anatomic.  Vertebral body heights are preserved.  The
marrow signal is diffusely T1 heterogeneous and replaced, compatible with
known history of multiple myeloma without evidence of focal lesion extending
into the epidural space or prevertebral soft tissues.  No marrow edema pattern
to suggest acute fracture.  The visualized posterior fossa is unremarkable. 
There is no definite cord signal abnormality.

C2-C3: No significant spinal canal narrowing.  Uncovertebral facet arthropathy
results in mild right no significant left neural foraminal narrowing.

C3-C4: Central protrusion with intervertebral osteophytes results in severe
spinal canal narrowing, remodeling the cord without definitive underlying cord
signal change.  Uncovertebral and facet arthropathy results in severe left and
moderate to severe right neural foraminal narrowing.

C4-C5: Central protrusion with intervertebral osteophytes results in moderate
to severe spinal canal narrowing remodeling the cord.  Uncovertebral and facet
arthropathy results in severe bilateral neural foraminal narrowing.

C5-C6: A central protrusion and intervertebral osteophytes results in severe
spinal canal narrowing, remodeling the cord without definitive underlying cord
signal change.  Uncovertebral and facet arthropathy results in severe left and
moderate to severe right neural foraminal narrowing.

C6-C7: Central protrusion results in mild spinal canal narrowing. 
Uncovertebral and facet arthropathy results in severe bilateral neural
foraminal narrowing.

C7-T1: Central protrusion does not significantly narrow spinal canal.  Facet
arthropathy results in severe left and mild right neural foraminal narrowing.

Atrophy of the right submandibular gland is identified, otherwise the
remainder the visualized prevertebral and paraspinal soft tissues are
unremarkable.  Right Port-A-Cath is identified.

THORACIC:
Thoracic alignment is anatomic.  Vertebral body heights are preserved.  The
marrow signal is diffusely T1 heterogeneous without evidence of expansile soft
tissue lesion extending into the epidural space or prevertebral soft tissues. 
Mild anterior wedge shapes of the lower thoracic spine spanning T9 through T12
is unchanged from prior examination, chronic in nature.  The remainder of the
vertebral body heights are preserved.  No marrow edema pattern to suggest
acute fracture.

There is no abnormal signal of the cord.

No high-grade spinal canal or neural foraminal narrowing.

Left small to moderate pleural effusion.  T2 hyperintense cystic lesions of
the right kidney measuring up to 1.6 cm are statistically most likely simple
cysts.  The remainder the visualized prevertebral paraspinal soft tissues are
grossly unremarkable.

LUMBAR:
There is mild kyphotic angulation of the thoracolumbar junction secondary to
anterior wedge shapes of T11 and T12, unchanged from prior examination. 
Lumbar alignment is anatomic.  Mild anterior wedge shapes of the L1 through L4
vertebral bodies as well as L5 superior endplate Schmorl's node is unchanged
from prior examination.  There is transitional anatomy of S1 with a S1-S2
disc.  The marrow signal is diffusely T1 heterogeneous, without evidence of
expansile lesion encroaching into the spinal canal or prevertebral soft
tissues.  There is no signal abnormality of the terminal cord.

L1-L2: Small disc bulge does not narrow the spinal canal or neural foramina.

L2-L3: A disc bulge with thickening of the ligamentum flavum results in
moderate spinal canal narrowing.  There is mild bilateral neural foraminal
narrowing.

L3-L4 through L5-S1: Small disc bulges do not significantly narrow the spinal
canal.  In combination with facet arthropathy, there is mild-to-moderate
bilateral L4-L5 and L5-S1 neural foraminal narrowing.

S1-S2: A disc bulge does not significantly narrow the spinal canal.  In
combination with facet arthropathy, there is mild-to-moderate bilateral neural
foraminal narrowing.

Visualized prevertebral and paraspinal soft tissues are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:


1. The marrow signal is diffusely heterogeneous without evidence of expansile
lytic lesion extending into the epidural space or prevertebral soft tissues,
compatible with patient's history of multiple myeloma.
2. Multilevel lower thoracic and lumbar anterior wedge shapes of the vertebral
bodies, unchanged from CTA chest, abdomen and pelvis of ___,
chronic in nature.  No definite marrow signal edema pattern to suggest acute
fracture.
3. There is severe spinal canal narrowing secondary to degenerative changes in
the cervical spine at C3-C4 and C5-C6, which flattens the cord without
underlying cord signal change.  Multilevel severe neural foraminal narrowing
of the cervical spine identified.
4. There is no high-grade spinal canal or neural foraminal narrowing of the
thoracic spine.
5. Moderate spinal canal narrowing at L2-L3.  Otherwise, no high-grade spinal
canal narrowing of the lumbar spine.  Mild-to-moderate bilateral neural
foraminal narrowing spanning L4-L5 through S1-S2.
6. There is no abnormal cord signal.
7. Additional findings as described above.
